question: Should OpenClaw core own a scheduled live Strategic Director eval workflow that hydrates provider/Codex secrets, or should this branch be split so deterministic contracts land separately first?
rationale: The workflow direction changes recurring maintainer automation and secret exposure boundaries, which code repair alone cannot decide safely.

options.title: Split deterministic contracts first
options.body: Land the deterministic harness and Strategic Director contracts after the narrower blockers are fixed, and review secret-bearing live scheduling in a later maintainer-sponsored PR.

options.title: Sponsor the live workflow after hardening
options.body: Keep the live workflow in scope only if maintainers explicitly accept scheduled secret-backed evals after action refs, Docker image, config/model contracts, and proof are fixed.

options.title: Pause this draft branch
options.body: Leave or close the draft until the contributor can provide proof and a maintainer-editable, rebased branch.

recommendation.title: Split deterministic contracts first
recommendation.body: Land the deterministic harness and Strategic Director contracts after the narrower blockers are fixed, and review secret-bearing live scheduling in a later maintainer-sponsored PR.

likelyOwner.reason: History shows broad adjacent ownership across the workflow, scripts, model-selection, and config surfaces, making this the best available routing candidate for the security/product boundary choice.
